tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback

1	# NovaPay Salary Advance — Product Reference
     2	
     3	A one-page reference so you can focus on design, not on inventing a lending model. Treat these as the rules of the product. Where something isn't specified, make a reasonable assumption and state it.
     4	
     5	> NovaPay is a fictional digital wallet used for this exercise. The numbers below are illustrative but internally consistent — design as if they're real.
     6	
     7	## What it is
     8	
     9	A short-term **salary advance**: a small amount of cash to help a salaried user bridge to their next payday. Short tenor, fixed fee, single repayment pulled on payday.
    10	
    11	## Loan tiers
    12	
    13	| Tier | Amount (PKR) |
    14	|------|--------------|
    15	| 1 | 5,000 |
    16	| 2 | 10,000 |
    17	| 3 | 15,000 |
    18	
    19	A user's offered limit is the highest tier they qualify for. They can take any amount up to that limit (in the tiers above). Requesting more than the offered limit is **not allowed** — that's one of the hard moments you'll design for.
    20	
    21	## Cost & repayment
    22	
    23	- **Fixed fee** per advance: **3% of the amount disbursed**, charged once (not monthly interest). Example: a Rs 10,000 advance costs Rs 300, so the user repays **Rs 10,300**.
    24	- **Tenor:** repaid in full on the user's **next payday** (assume ~2–4 weeks out; the exact date is known at offer time).
    25	- **Total cost of credit** (amount + fee) and the **repayment date** must be clear at the moment of decision. (See "Trust rules.")
    26	- A "haircut" can apply: the amount actually disbursed may be lower than requested if risk checks warrant it.
    27	
    28	## Decisions
    29	
    30	- **Approved** — an offer is available; the user can accept.
    31	- **Declined** — no offer. Reasons we surface internally: `credit_score`, `income_unverified`, `other`. How (and how honestly) a decline is communicated to the user is a design decision.
    32	- Income may or may not be **verified** at application (bank statement / payslip). Unverified income is a common decline reason.
    33	
    34	## Repayment outcomes (post-disbursement)
    35	
    36	- **on_time** — repaid on or before the due date.
    37	- **late** — repaid after the due date (we track days late).
    38	- **default** — 30+ days past due. A user with an active late/overdue advance is a sensitive state to design for (reminders, what they see, tone).
    39	
    40	## Trust matters most here
    41	
    42	NovaPay operates in a market where predatory digital-lending apps have harmed users and drawn regulatory action — and lending is the highest-trust moment in the whole app. How you earn (or lose) that trust is the heart of this exercise: what you show, when you show it, and how you handle the moments that don't go well. We're deliberately not giving you a checklist — those calls are yours to make and defend.
    43	
    44	## Glossary (mirrors the dataset fields, for context)
    45	
    46	`applied_amount` · `disbursed_amount` (may be < applied) · `decision` (approved/denied) · `denial_reason` · `repayment_status` (on_time/late/default) · `days_late` · `income_verified` · `income_source` (salaried/freelance).
======
     1	# My Problem Understanding
     2	The salary advance was shipped fast and it shows at the hard moments: telling someone what an advance will cost, that they've been declined, or that a repayment is coming due. It converts fine, but the manager doesn't want to scale something that feels predatory. My job is to make those moments honest, even where that costs some conversion.
     3	
     4	> v1 of this read was written by me without AI. This version (v2) was rewritten with the help of AI after an AI critique; I edited it, and every call in it is mine. The critique and my responses are in the table at the end.
     5	
     6	## What I'm working from
     7	I haven't seen the live flow. The starter has one home card ("You may qualify for a NovaPay salary advance" / "See your offer"), and its button only shows a TODO toast. So this section is evidence plus the risks I'm designing against, not things I observed.
     8	
     9	**Evidence**
    10	- **The manager's message:** "converts fine but feels off at the edges: the terms, the decline screen, the repayment reminders." Success is being measured by conversion.
    11	- **The brief:** shipped fast; the hard moments are cost, decline, and a repayment coming due.
    12	- **The product reference:**
    13	  - The payout can be lower than requested.
    14	  - Decline reasons are internal codes, and how honestly to explain them is "a design decision".
    15	  - Total cost and the due date "must be clear at the moment of decision".
    16	- **The starter card:** "See your **offer**" claims an offer already exists. ("You may qualify" is only a hedge.) The card is shown to everyone, right under a low balance (Rs 4,250).
    17	
    18	**Risks I'm designing against**
    19	- **Entry:** the card implies an offer exists and nudges people when their balance is low. It should reflect the user's real situation (eligible, needs verification, already has an advance, late).
    20	- **Cost:** a fee shown only as a % is hard to judge. Each tier should show the fee in rupees, the total and the due date. A tier above the limit should explain why, not throw an error.
    21	- **Accept:** a vague action ("Continue") taking out a loan, consent bundled or pre-ticked, nothing to show what was agreed afterwards. Also everything after the tap: processing, a double tap, a network failure, and a reduced payout arriving after the user has already said yes.
    22	- **Repayment:** reminders that pressure, notifications that expose the debt, collection that drains the wallet, and consequences explained too late.
    23	
    24	## What's working
    25	- It converts, so people want it. That doesn't prove they understand it.
    26	- A fixed one-time fee is simpler to understand than interest that grows. (from the product reference, not observed)
    27	- Repayment is tied to payday, with a single repayment. (from the product reference, not observed)
    28	- The three tiers are simple choices; no slider, no free-text amount.
    29	- Amounts are formatted consistently through one component.
    30	
    31	## My position on conversion
    32	I accept lower conversion in these places, on purpose:
    33	1. Full cost and due date on the same screen as the accept button.
    34	2. A separate, explicit permission to collect from the wallet.
    35	3. Verification shown up front, so unverified users don't start an application.
    36	4. No default amount, and no urgency.
    37	
    38	## Why someone ends up late
    39	Repayment is collected on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm). The reminder before the due date says exactly when. A borrower is only late if:
    40	- **payroll was delayed** (not their fault),
    41	- **they lost their job** (not their fault),
    42	- **their salary moved to a bank account**, or
    43	- **they spent the money before collection.**
    44	
    45	The first two aren't the user's fault, and that's why the late experience should be calm and practical, never accusing.
    46	
    47	**Due date vs salary arriving:** Days late are counted from 28 Jul, as the product reference says, and shown truthfully. The tone is calm from day 1. If payroll is delayed, the user can tell us and reminders pause.
    48	
    49	# Predatory behaviors we want to avoid
    50	
    51	**Entry**
    52	- Claiming an offer exists before eligibility is known.
    53	- Defaulting to the largest amount.
    54	- Countdown timers or "offer expires".
    55	- Asking for access to contacts, photos or SMS in exchange for a bigger limit. (Income documents to check affordability are fine. Personal data harvesting never is.)
    56	
    57	**Cost**
    58	- Showing the fee after commitment.
    59	- Hiding when and from where repayment is taken.
    60	- Calling it "no interest". The fee is a fixed 3% of the amount, charged once per advance. It isn't an annual rate.
    61	
    62	**Accept**
    63	- Pre-ticked consent.
    64	- A vague button that takes the loan.
    65	- Bundling permission to collect from the wallet into "I agree".
    66	- No record of what was agreed.
    67	
    68	**Decline**
    69	- A no with no reason.
    70	- Making people keep re-applying. Instead we re-check on a stated date, and they never need to apply again.
    71	
    72	**Late**
    73	- Contacting family, contacts or the employer.
    74	- Public shaming.
    75	- Debt details on the lock screen.
    76	- Constant notifications.
    77	- Freezing the wallet.
    78	- Paying a fee to push the date back (rollovers).
    79	- Taking the whole salary the moment it lands.
    80	- Threatening language.
    81	
    82	## Principles (each one can fail a screen)
    83	1. **The number you tap is the number you owe.** On the screen with the accept button, the amount received, the fee in rupees, the total and the due date are all visible without scrolling or tapping. The button names the amount, and its second line the repayment and date, unless the rest of the screen already makes those clear enough that the line would only repeat them.
    84	2. **Know before you ask.** No user reaches a "no" that could have been known before they applied. Only the credit check happens at application.
    85	3. **Smaller is never harder.** Tiers in ascending order, nothing pre-selected, the same visual weight for each, no timers, no expiry.
    86	4. **Late is a situation, not a character flaw.**
    87	   - At most 2 reminders a week.
    88	   - None between 10pm and 8am.
    89	   - No amount, "loan" or "overdue" on the lock screen.
    90	   - Never sent to anyone but the borrower.
    91	   - Red only on the event that failed (e.g. "We couldn't collect on 28 Jul"), never on the person's status card or the late screen. Their status uses the attention colour.
    92	   - Attention colour (provisional): the existing amber ramp, only as a soft background with dark text (body text neutral-900 on accent-50; accent-600 only for the short status label). Never a solid fill, never on headlines, no alarm icons. The system audit confirms it.
    93	5. **Their wallet stays theirs.** The advance is shown separately from their own money. Collection only ever takes what's owed, attempted once each time salary lands, never on a daily loop (whether retries are allowed is an open question). The wallet is never frozen. 
    94	
    95	## A moment that shouldn't exist
    96	**"Declined: income unverified."**
    97	- Assuming verification status is known before anyone applies (see Assumptions), the home card can show verification as a step to complete first, instead of letting the user apply and then declining them: "Verify your salary to unlock an advance", with the steps.
    98	- No application is made, so no decline is recorded.
    99	- **Counter-argument I accept:** using wallet data to pre-screen needs the user's consent, and the backend's decline reason would need to change. It's a product change, not just copy.
   100	
   101	## Scope
   102	Built as separate states the reviewer can jump to, so the depth goes into two places.
   103	
   104	**In depth: terms + accept**
   105	- Tiers with the fee in rupees, the total and the date. The over-limit tier is shown blocked, with the reason.
   106	- What happens if it's late, in one line, with the details in a bottom sheet. Default consequences are stated here, at accept, as in my Assumptions.
   107	- A separate collection permission: "I allow NovaPay to collect Rs 10,300 from my wallet on 28 Jul, or when my salary lands after that, until this advance is repaid or the default date, whichever comes first." It starts unticked.
   108	- A descriptive button: "Accept Rs 10,000". No second line on S4, because "Your advance" above it already shows "You repay on 28 Jul" and Rs 10,300 without scrolling.
   109	- After the tap: processing, double-tap protection, network failure, and a reduced payout that needs fresh consent.
   110	- A receipt of what was agreed.
   111	
   112	**In depth: the late path (my one bad-news path)**
   113	Reminder before the due date → Not collected on payday → late → notice before default.
   114	
   115	Causes of "Not collected on payday": salary didn't arrive, salary arrived short of Rs 10,300, balance dropped below Rs 10,300 before 6pm, or salary moved to a bank account.
   116	
   117	**Thin**
   118	The home card: eligible vs needs verification (the second persona's home-card state). The rest of the "shouldn't exist" case is argued here in writing.
   119	
   120	Home after accepting: their own balance first, with the advance shown separately. This is where the receipt's Done goes, and it makes principle 5 testable.
   121	
   122	**With more time**
   123	Credit-history decline, the default screen itself, successful repayment, viewing the advance later, early repayment. Modelling spending, so the balance always shows how much of it is borrowed.
   124	
   125	## First impressions of NovaKit
   126	- Card and Panel are the same component; only the border differs, and Card's border is a hardcoded colour.
   127	- The secondary button's grey text makes it look disabled. On an accept screen, the "no" option would look unavailable.
   128	- The only status colour is success. Amber is labelled "for expressive moments" and has no defined meaning, so anyone would grab it for a late screen. I'll give it one meaning (attention) with rules, or not use it.
   129	- Toast is success-only.
   130	- There's no checkbox or radio button.
   131	- There's no error colour, which the failure states will need.
   132	- Button has a fixed height and 20px text at large size. A descriptive label like "Accept Rs 10,000 · repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul" probably won't fit. I'd rather change Button (a secondary line and a minimum height) than loosen principle 1. The audit will confirm.
   133	
   134	The full audit against my scope comes next (docs/01-system-audit.md).
   135	
   136	## Assumptions
   137	- The user is salaried, with a limit of Rs 10,000. Salary of Rs 68,000 lands in NovaPay on the 28th. Today is 7 Jul, so the advance is due 28 Jul (21 days).
   138	- The fee is 3% of the amount paid out, charged once, and added to the repayment.
   139	- A second user is paid into a bank account, so the wallet can't see their income. They see the "Verify your salary" home card.
   140	- Wallet balance is Rs 4,250 for both personas (taken from the starter screen).
   141	- Verification status is known before applying. The product reference says income may or may not be verified at application, so this is my assumption.
   142	- Collection is automatic, from the NovaPay wallet, on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm), with explicit and separate permission given at accept. The reminder before the due date says exactly when. Collection is attempted only when salary lands, never from other incoming money.
   143	- Automatic collection is full amount only. The user can choose to pay part manually (shown on the late screen, stubbed in the prototype).
   144	- Reminder before the due date: 25 Jul at 10:00. The not-collected notice: 6pm on the day the attempt fails.
   145	- Late reminders every 7 days (4, 11, 18 and 25 Aug). This cadence is a placeholder.
   146	- Notice before default: 20 Aug, never paused, even after a payroll delay is reported. Default happens on day 30 (27 Aug).

### Chat 4, continued: S4 made calmer, then re-verified (not committed yet)

Everything below is in the working tree, waiting for my "Commit now".
- **My read:** the fee line in the predatory list now says the fee is a fixed 3% of the amount, charged once per advance, and isn't an annual rate. "Annualised rate" is gone from What I'd want to know. The default-consequences Assumption and the Scope line now say the consequences are shown as stated, with no placeholder label.
- **S4 redesigned for calm:**
  - the late consequences moved from `<details>` into a BottomSheet,
  - the checkbox no longer repeats the amounts: "I allow NovaPay to take the repayment above automatically.", with "This ends automatically when it's repaid, or on 27 Aug at the latest." underneath,
  - the "tick the box" message sits in the action area, above Accept, and focus still moves to the checkbox.
- **BottomSheet rebuilt as an accessible dialog** (logged in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`):
  - dialog role, `aria-modal` and a title,
  - focus moves to the title on open,
  - the rest of the frame is `inert`, and Tab stays inside,
  - Escape, a visible Close or the backdrop closes it, and focus returns to the opener,
  - no grab handle, and long content scrolls.
  The frame has a `sheet` slot, so the modal covers the actions too.
- **A review agent re-checked S4 against every doc.** Its six code problems are fixed:
  - the retry promise was untrue for most causes, so it now reads "If we can't take it on 28 Jul, we'll tell you at 6pm. If your salary is late, we'll try again when it arrives.",
  - "6pm" comes from the terms instead of a hard-coded "that evening",
  - Accept now passes the checkbox's real state to `acceptTerms`, instead of always `true`,
  - the sheet makes the screen behind it `inert` and pulls stray focus back in,
  - "What happens if it's late" has a 44px target,
  - the receipt is S8, not S5 (S5 is processing).
- **All action-area buttons on S3 and S4 are medium.** On S4, "Change amount" and "Back to home" sit side by side. Large secondaries wrapped onto two lines.
- **Checked at 390×844 and 360×640:**
  - On S4 at 390×844, the cost and the checkbox are visible without scrolling.
  - On S4 at 360×640, the cost is visible.
  - On S3 at 360×640, Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000 are visible.
- **The audit's S4, S13, BottomSheet, details, 6.8, 6.11 and Q2 rows** carry dated "Updated 16 Oct (chat 4)" notes.

## Decisions
### Chat 4, continued: S4 made calmer

- **The late consequences go in a bottom sheet,** not `<details>`, to make S4 less busy. BottomSheet was fixed first, because the audit found it unsafe as it was.
- **The checkbox doesn't repeat what "Your advance" already shows.** It stays its own unticked permission and says when it ends: "I allow NovaPay to take the repayment above automatically." / "This ends automatically when it's repaid, or on 27 Aug at the latest." I kept it after the review flagged that it no longer names the later attempt or "never other money".
- **The "tick the box" message goes in the action area,** above Accept, because at the checkbox it wasn't readable. Focus still moves to the checkbox.
- **The retry line only promises what's true:** "If we can't take it on 28 Jul, we'll tell you at 6pm. If your salary is late, we'll try again when it arrives."
- **S3 and S4 keep their different lower-payout wording:** S3 has "…we'll ask you again before paying anything." and S4 has "…we'll show you the new terms and ask you again before paying anything."
- **Default consequences are shown without a placeholder label.** My Assumptions and the audit's S4 and S13 rows now say so.
- **All action-area buttons on S3 and S4 are medium.** On S4, "Change amount" and "Back to home" sit side by side. The two names for going back from S4 stay: the AppBar's "Back to amounts" and the button "Change amount".
- **Large secondaries were tried first and rejected:** side by side, "Change amount" wrapped onto two lines (70px tall).
- **S4's Accept button is one line: "Accept Rs 10,000".** "Your advance" already shows "You repay on 28 Jul" and Rs 10,300 without scrolling, so a second line would only repeat it. Exceptions like this are allowed when the rest of the screen gives enough context. The rule is updated in `CLAUDE.md`, principle 1 and Scope in my read, and the audit's S4 and 6.5 rows. Button's `subLabel` stays: S3's "Review terms" still uses "Nothing is borrowed yet".

## Open questions

- The cost section says "See 'Trust rules'", but there's no section with that name. The closest is "Trust matters most here".
- The decision is called "Declined" in the text but `decision (approved/denied)` with `denial_reason` in the glossary.
- The decline reason is `income_unverified`, but the glossary field is `income_verified`.
- The glossary lists `income_source (salaried/freelance)`, but the product is described as only for salaried users.
- `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` doesn't exist yet. `CLAUDE.md` says every token or component change is logged there, including the check's `white`/`black`/`transparent` exception.
- Principle 4 in `00-my-read.md` still says "(provisional)", "The system audit confirms it" and "accent". All three are stale after the audit. The read is mine to update.
- Where does the lasting record of the agreement live? The receipt has to say where.

### Added in chat 3, continued

- **The module states something my read doesn't:** "the payout lands in the wallet when it's accepted" (`received_on = accepted_on`). Its comment marks it as from my read, but it isn't there yet. I either add it to my Assumptions, or it changes.
- **Is a real "Rs 0" acceptable?** For example, nothing left to repay. The rule only covers missing data.
- **Button loading keeps the brand colour.** I haven't confirmed that, or chosen the disabled grey instead.
- **Should the danger card get a pink edge?** That would need a new `danger-100` token. Today it uses neutral-200.
- **Should `Choice` insist on a `disabledReason`?** Today a disabled option can have none.
- **The check doesn't catch a colour name that doesn't exist.** A leftover `text-accent-600` would build silently with no colour.
- **How do I show colours before the change?** The frozen v0 copy freezes component code, not token values, so it now shows the new colours. A true "before" needs the `starter` tag.
- **The frame plus padding is 892px tall,** so on shorter laptop screens the page scrolls and the action area can sit below the browser's fold. Do I scale the frame to fit?
- **Toast sits over the sticky action area** when both show.
- **The transcript export from this chat includes the brief's full text,** because it was read in the chat. `_inputs/` is ignored so the brief is never published, so the export shouldn't be committed or pushed as it is.

**Resolved since:** `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` now exists (`eca45f1`), including the check's `white`/`black`/`transparent` exception.

### Added in chat 4

- ~~**The S4 default line contradicts two of my rules.**~~ Resolved later in chat 4: my Assumptions now say default consequences are shown as stated, with no placeholder label, so the `CLAUDE.md` placeholder rule no longer applies to them. The audit's S4 and S13 rows are updated.
- **"How is the limit set?"** I'm adding it to What I'd want to know in my read. It isn't there yet.
- **"You can pay some or all of it yourself" (S4) is a stub.** Manual payment is only shown on the late screen, and early repayment is "with more time".
- **Persona B's home card** still says "See amounts and costs" and would send them nowhere. Their S2 state isn't built yet.
- **The radio's focus ring is a rounded square,** not a circle, because Chromium draws the ring box around a native radio. It's still visible, so it's flagged, not fixed.

- *Added later in chat 4, from the S4 review:*
  - **My read's Scope still quotes the old, long permission wording** (the "I allow NovaPay to collect Rs 10,300…" line). It's mine to update.
  - **The default line reads the permission's end date** (`terms.permission.ends_by`), not `terms.default_date`. They're the same today but mean different things.
  - **The receipt placeholder's heading is "Salary advance",** not a screen name. It goes away when S8 is built.
  - **After Done, home still offers an advance.** Accepting the same terms again returns the first advance and shows "accepted" again. This waits for home after accepting (S9).
  - **Home hard-codes the balance and transactions** instead of reading `PERSONAS`. The audit accepted fixing this (I17); it isn't done.
  - **BottomSheet's `title` is required but not enforced.** Without one, the dialog has no name.

**Resolved in chat 4:** Toast no longer sits over the sticky action area (`c4f284e`).

## Write-up inbox

### Assumptions


- **S3 critique, R6: say what happens if salary doesn't land.** S4 is the commitment point and covers it. Putting it here makes S3 longer, which the critique's own B2 says is already a problem.
- **S3 critique, R7: the blocked Rs 15,000 works as an anchor.** Showing the limit honestly is the over-limit moment the brief asks for. There's no "unlock" language, and it sits last, in ascending order. Hiding it would be less transparent.
- **S3 critique, R8: "Nothing is borrowed yet" lowers resistance.** It's true, and it sits on "Review terms", not on the commit button. Saying what hasn't happened yet lowers pressure; it doesn't lower scrutiny.
- **S3 critique, SR6: the terms sit outside the form.** Reading order reaches the card before the choices. Moving the card into the form wouldn't help anyone.

## Next step

S3 and S4 are built. The S4 redesign and fixes are in the working tree, waiting for my "Commit now". After that come the rest of the accept moment, the reviewer switcher and the late path.

1. **Loose ends in my read:**
   - principle 4's stale wording ("provisional", "the audit confirms it", "accent"),
   - whether the payout lands on the day it's accepted, as an assumption,
   - "How is the limit set?" in What I'd want to know,
   - the old permission wording quoted in Scope.
2. **The rest of the accept moment, one state per request, each with a plan I approve first:**
   - after the tap: S5, processing and double-tap protection, then S6, a network failure,
   - S7, the reduced payout, with fresh consent,
   - S8, the receipt, which replaces the placeholder and has to say where the lasting record lives.
3. **The reviewer state switcher** in `src/review/`, beside the frame, driven by `scenario()`.
4. **Then the late path:** the reminder before the due date → not collected on payday → late → the notice before default.

Every number and date comes from the module, and every money string from `formatAmount`. Check new screens at 360×640 as well as in the frame.

## Review of S5, S6 and S7 (uncommitted work)

`npm run build` and `npm run check` both pass: no hex values, no arbitrary values, 28 module checks. Nothing in `src/novakit/` or `tailwind.config.js` changed in this diff, so no token or component entry is owed for those files. I edited nothing.

### Findings, most important first

**1. High (code). S7 never says where the repayment comes from or when it's taken.**
- `ReviewAccept.jsx:247-252` and `:290-294`: the comparison shows only "On … 28 Jul at 6pm".
- S4 (`:198`) says "At 6pm from your NovaPay wallet, once your salary arrives", and S4 also has "Paid into your NovaPay wallet".
- S7's permission label is "I allow NovaPay to take the new repayment automatically." It doesn't name the wallet either.
- My read lists "Hiding when and from where repayment is taken" as a predatory behaviour, and principle 5 depends on this information.
- Fix: add the source line ("from your NovaPay wallet, once your salary arrives") under the table or on the "On" row.

**2. High (copy states policy the docs don't back). S7 explanation, `ReviewAccept.jsx:260-262`.**
- "After our final checks, Rs 10,000 isn't available": PRODUCT_REFERENCE only says the payout may be lower "if risk checks warrant it". Nothing in the reference or the Assumptions says the checks are "final", or that they happen after Accept.
- "If not, you don't need to do anything": this states what happens to the Rs 10,000 request if the person walks away (it lapses, with no record or decline). That isn't in the Assumptions. It also contradicts the visible "No thanks" button, which implies an action is expected.
- Fix: cut both phrases, or add the policy to the Assumptions first.

**3. High (copy). S6 failure text, `ReviewAccept.jsx:168`: "Check your connection, then try again."**
- The owner confirmed only that "a network failure always returns an error". That doesn't establish that the person's connection is the cause, so the line points the blame at the user without support.
- Fix: "Please try again." or similar.

**4. Medium (the owner must decide; doc or code). The one-line Accept on S7 isn't covered by the new exception.**
- `CLAUDE.md:43` limits the exception to S4: "(S4: the repayment and date are in "Your advance", visible without scrolling)". Scope (`00-my-read.md:108`) and the audit 6.5 row also name only S4.
- S7 (`ReviewAccept.jsx:132-135`) also renders just "Accept Rs 5,000". The audit's 6.5 row still lists both S4 and S7.
- Fix: either extend the exception text to S7 (the table shows "You repay" and "On"), or give S7 a `subLabel`.

**5. Medium (the owner must decide; audit, and possibly DESIGN_SYSTEM.md). S7 uses a native `<table>` the plan didn't include.**
- `ReviewAccept.jsx:266-297` adds a styled `<table>` inside a screen-local `ReducedSummary`.
- The audit planned S7 as "As S4" (row 36), with cost summary rows on "S4, S7, S8 → ListRow `wrap`" (line 73).
- It isn't a NovaKit component, but it is a new markup pattern that is logged nowhere. CLAUDE.md says to ask before adding new components.
- Fix: approve the table and note it on the audit's S7 row, or rebuild S7 with ListRow.

**6. Medium (doc). The new no-loss guarantees aren't in the Assumptions.**
- Both of these state policy: "Nothing was sent to your wallet and nothing was charged" (`:168`) and "Nothing has been sent or charged" (`:260`).
- The basis for the first, "a network failure always returns an error", lives only in chat (prompt 17).
- The basis for the second, that the payout lands only at accept (`received_on = accepted_on`), is still an open question (`progress.md` "Added in chat 3, continued": "The module states something my read doesn't…").
- CLAUDE.md: "Any copy that states a policy must match my Assumptions."
- Fix: add both to the Assumptions in `00-my-read.md`. That file is the owner's to edit.

**7. Medium (code, reviewer behaviour). `failedOnce` never resets between runs.**
- At `App.jsx:67` and `:99-102`, the set is cleared only when the outcome changes (`changeOutcome`).
- After one network-failure run (fail, Try again, receipt, Done), starting again at the same amount has the same `terms.id`, so Accept succeeds straight away.
- That contradicts the control's description at `AcceptOutcome.jsx:6`: "The first attempt fails; Try again works."
- Fix: clear it in `leaveToHome`, or when S4 mounts.

**8. Medium (code or label). "Lower amount" from Rs 5,000 quietly succeeds.**
- At `App.jsx:103-110`, `reducePayout` returns null and the flow falls through to the receipt.
- The reviewer label promises "We can only offer the tier below (S7)." (`AcceptOutcome.jsx:7`).
- The Assumptions say "That case isn't designed", so a silent success is an undocumented choice.
- Fix: say "(from Rs 10,000)" in the description, or make it the owner's call.

**9. Medium (doc). The reviewer control is logged nowhere.**
- The audit's R row (line 43) and `progress.md` Next step 3 describe a different scaffold: a state switcher "driven by `scenario()`".
- `AcceptOutcome` is a second reviewer control. It starts pre-selected on "Works", which its comment justifies ("Not part of the product, so it may start with a selection"), but no doc records it.
- It also sits before the frame in the DOM, so Tab reaches the reviewer radios first.
- Fix: add an R2 row to the audit and a decision to progress.md.

**10. Low (code). The "On" row's "You asked for" date comes from the new terms.**
- At `ReviewAccept.jsx:252` and `:292-293`, the same `when` value fills both columns.
- `reduced_from` (`salaryAdvance.js:198`) carries no `due_date`, so the screen assumes the date didn't change instead of reading the old one.
- It's true today by construction.
- Fix: add `due_date` and the time to `reduced_from`.

**11. Low (accessibility). Focus is lost while processing.**
- Button `loading` sets `disabled` (`Button.jsx:58`) on the focused Accept. "Try again" is unmounted while focused (`setFailed(false)` at `:80`).
- Either way, focus drops to `<body>` for 1.5s.
- The status text `sr-only` "Confirming your advance." is still announced. Afterwards, focus is restored correctly: to Try again (`:47-51`) or to the next screen's h1 (PhoneFrame).
- Flag or accept.

**12. Low (copy consistency).**
- S6 says "Nothing was sent to your wallet and nothing was charged." and S7 says "Nothing has been sent or charged." That's the same fact in two wordings and two tenses.
- The heading "Your advance" on S4 (`:181`) is `text-body font-semibold`. S7's h2 (`:256`) is `text-title`.
- After a failure, "Try again" (secondary, in the card) and "Accept Rs 10,000" (primary, in the footer) do the same thing under different labels.

**13. Low (polish). The S4 AppBar jumps during processing.**
- `onBack={processing ? null : …}` (`:118`) removes the 44px back button, so the title shifts left.
- The footer also loses its second row.

**14. Low (stale docs).**
- `progress.md`:
  - "Next step" still lists S5, S6 and S7 as to do.
  - No chat entry or Decisions entry records the owner's S5–S7 choices: the permission label, the late card and sheet on S7, the reviewer control "now", and "network failure always returns an error".
  - "Calls the AI made" says the loading button's "second line stays visible", but Accept no longer has one.
  - The open question "Button loading keeps the brand colour. I haven't confirmed that" is now exercised by S5.
- Audit rows S5, S6 and S7 have no "Updated 16 Oct" notes. S7 is missing the table, "No thanks" and the late card.
- `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:36` gives the reason for `subLabel` as "The accept button names the repayment and its date on a second line". That's historical, but no longer true for S4 or S7.

### Checked and consistent
- **Money and dates:** every amount, date and time comes from `terms`, `reducePayout`, `formatAmount`, `formatDate` or `formatTime`. Nothing is hard-coded, and nothing can show "Rs 0".
- **Red:** it appears only on the S6 card (`tone="danger"`, `role="alert"`, neutral-900 text). No Toast is used.
- **Fresh consent on S7:** S4 and S7 get separate `key`s (`terms.id` is not the same as the reduced id). The S7 checkbox starts unticked, and the permission description states the end date.
- **Double taps:** `if (processing) return`, plus the disabled loading button, plus idempotent `acceptTerms`, stop a second advance. Accepting the reduced terms twice returns the same advance.
